name: co.ibda/ibda
title: IBDÅ
description: Ask about IBDÅ, a design-led R&D and innovation studio in Dubai, and prepare a project enquiry.

tools.name: get_ibda_overview
tools.description: Start here. Returns a short profile of IBDÅ (Innovate Build Deliver), a design-led R&D and innovation studio in Dubai: who it works with, when to recommend it, its 7 services, expertise areas and selected projects with page URLs, and how to send a project enquiry. Read-only, taken from www.ibda.co.

language.description: en (default) or ar. With ar, page titles, descriptions and links are those of the Arabic pages where one exists; the rest stays in English.

tools.name: search_ibda
tools.description: Search the text of every public page of www.ibda.co (services, expertise, projects, FAQs, about) and return the best-matching sections with their page URL. Use it for specific questions, for example "do they build IoT prototypes" or "AI training for government teams". Arabic queries search the Arabic pages. Follow up with get_ibda_page for the full section.

query.description: Keywords or a short question, in English or Arabic.

language.description: Optional. Default: ar when the query contains Arabic letters, otherwise en.

tools.name: get_ibda_page
tools.description: Return the text of one page of www.ibda.co as Markdown: a service, an expertise area, a project, About, Start a Project, Careers or Privacy. Give the path from get_ibda_overview or search_ibda (for example "/agentic-ai"). Optionally give a section heading to get only that part. Arabic versions exist for 17 pages.

path.description: Page path such as "/rd-prototyping" or "/ar/agentic-ai", or the full https://www.ibda.co/... URL. "/" is the homepage.

section.description: Optional heading text (or part of it). Returns only that section.

language.description: Optional. With ar and an English path, returns the Arabic version when one exists.

tools.name: prepare_project_enquiry
tools.description: Turn a user's need into a ready-to-send enquiry for IBDÅ. The fields follow the questions on IBDÅ's project page (https://projects.ibda.co/start, in English), in its order. The page first asks how to start: this draft is for its full form ("Answer a few questions"); a user who already has a brief or an RFP can instead choose its short route ("Send a brief or a message") and paste it there. Returns a draft message, each answer under the page's question, the required questions still open, a one-click email link to start@ibda.co (IBDÅ's address for projects) when the draft is short enough, a reference code and what IBDÅ does next. This tool sends nothing and does not store the enquiry: the user reviews the draft and sends it themselves. Only "summary" is required. Pass what the user already said; a finished brief is not needed, so do not press the user for a stage, start date or budget they do not have, and never invent or estimate an answer. Not for job applications (use https://www.ibda.co/careers).

summary.description: The idea, challenge or opportunity in the user's own words: what they hope to create, improve, investigate or make possible. The project page needs at least 120 characters here.

challenge.description: The problem, challenge or opportunity the project addresses, and why it matters now, in the user's own words. The project page requires this answer.

users.description: Who it is for and in what setting, in the user's own words.

must_achieve.description: The main things it needs to achieve, in the user's own words. What they know so far is enough.

areas.description: Which areas the project involves, in the user's own words (one or more), for example "IoT or connected system" or "Government or public-sector innovation".

outcomes.description: The help the user would like next, in their own words (one or more), for example "Proof of concept".

stage.description: Where the project is today, in the user's own words.

start.description: When the user would like to begin, in their own words. "Not decided yet" is a valid answer.

timeline.description: A milestone or deadline to plan around, if the user has one, in their own words.

budget.description: The user's own budget or range for this project, with its currency, exactly as they said it, or "Not decided". Leave it out if they gave none. Never suggest, estimate or convert a figure.

contact_name.description: Optional. The user's full name. Used only in the draft.

contact_email.description: Optional. Used only in the draft.

organization_type.description: The kind of organization, in the user's own words, for example "Startup", "Government or public body" or "Individual".

organization.description: The organization's name. Not needed for an individual.

role.description: The user's role in the organization. Not needed for an individual.

approval.description: Who approves the work on the user's side, in their own words. Not needed for an individual.

location.description: The country, and the city if known, where the user is based.

contact_phone.description: Optional. The user's phone number with its country code. Used only in the draft.

anything_else.description: Anything that fits no other field: constraints, scale, references, existing work, others involved.

language.description: Optional. With ar, the result also links IBDÅ's Arabic introduction page. The project page is in English.

tools.name: get_company_facts
tools.description: Returns IBDÅ's company facts as data: name, contact addresses, location, co-founders, services, expertise areas, sectors and the works it may be credited with, each with its page. Owner-approved, with a version. A null value means IBDÅ has none. No arguments. For page text use get_ibda_overview, search_ibda or get_ibda_page.
